title: A Unified Description of Electron-Phonon Coupling and Ion Migration in Metal Halide Perovskites
authors: Bo Cai, Yan Yang, Yoshiki Sugai, Maddison Wiles, Dongxu He, Yang Yang, Junmin Xia, Shufen Chen, Carla Verdi, Siyu Chen, Nan Zhang, Ming-Gang Ju, Chao Liang, Julian A. Steele
abstract: The remarkable optoelectronic properties of metal halide perovskites are closely linked to their unusually soft and polar chemical bonds that enable both strong electron-phonon interactions and ion migration. Yet these two defining characteristics have largely been treated as independent consequences of the same underlying chemical bonding. Here we show that they originate from a common electronic-structure framework by developing a general description linking lattice dynamics, electron-phonon coupling, and halide ion migration across representative Pb-based, Sn-based, and double perovskites. Spectrally resolved phonon-mode contributions demonstrate that the low-frequency shearing modes dominate halide migration, whereas high-frequency stretching modes govern carrier scattering through the Fröhlich interaction in all three compositions. We introduce an orbital hybridization descriptor to unify these findings, which connects metal-halide bonding characteristics with the migration barrier energies and Fröhlich coupling strengths, indicating a cooperative evolution of these two properties. These findings provide a generalized microscopic mechanism for simultaneously optimizing charge and ionic transport in soft semiconductors.
summary: This work unifies the seemingly separate phenomena of ion migration and electron-phonon coupling in metal halide perovskites using an orbital hybridization descriptor, $R$. By showing that both processes are governed by the same underlying electronic structure parameter, the authors propose a generalized mechanism for designing soft semiconductors with optimized charge and ionic transport simultaneously.
main_problem: The research aims to develop a unified microscopic description linking lattice dynamics, electron-phonon coupling (EPC), and ion migration in metal halide perovskites.
main_result: A single orbital hybridization descriptor ($R$) was introduced to show that both ionic transport barriers and EPC strengths arise from the same underlying electronic structure framework. This suggests a cooperative mechanism for optimizing charge and ionic transport simultaneously.
method: The study employs Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations, utilizing an orbital hybridization descriptor derived from a dual-atom model to quantify how lattice displacements modulate electronic coupling.
model_or_system: The physical system is Metal Halide Perovskites ($	ext{CsPbI}_3$, $	ext{CsSnI}_3$, and double perovskites). The theoretical framework uses an orbital hybridization descriptor $R = 2V / |\Delta E|$ to model the coupling between metal and halide orbitals.
key_observables: Electron-phonon coupling strength ($\Gamma_{e-	ext{ph}}$), ion migration barrier energies ($E_b$), and the orbital hybridization descriptor ($R$).
important_parameters: The relative values of $R$ across different perovskite compositions (e.g., $	ext{Cs}_2	ext{AgBiBr}_6 > 	ext{Sn-I} > 	ext{Pb-I}$), and the dependence of $R$ on specific phonon modes (stretching vs. shearing).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the descriptor $R$ acts as a universal electronic parameter governing both lattice restoring forces (migration) and dielectric screening (EPC). Calculations are often performed on archetypal cubic phases.
figures_summary: Figures conceptually link the hybridization descriptor $R$ to phonon modes: low-frequency shearing modes govern ion migration, while high-frequency stretching modes govern carrier scattering via the Fröhlich interaction. Supplementary figures detail how $R$ changes under specific atomic displacements (shortening/elongating bonds).
paper_structure: The paper establishes a conceptual framework linking bonding to dynamics using $R$. It then systematically calculates and analyzes how perturbing bond lengths or angles modulates $R$, which in turn dictates both the ion migration barrier and the EPC strength across multiple perovskite types.
why_interesting: While not directly focused on quantum information, the rigorous theoretical coupling of lattice vibrations (phonons) to electronic structure parameters ($R$) provides a powerful model for understanding strongly coupled open quantum systems where environment interaction dictates transport properties.
